source.title: Future Token Prediction - Causal Language Modelling with Per-Token Semantic State Vector for Multi-Token Prediction

record.tranche_reason: The study probes frozen model states for future-token prediction, a different method from the cited Future Lens work but aimed at future-token decodability.
record.gate_note: The GPT MLP-probe results in section 5.2 bear on future-token decodability. FTP models are trained explicitly with a multi-token prediction objective, so their results do not establish naturally occurring pre-caching in a next-token-only model. The study does not intervene on candidate future tokens or test rhyme planning. Text-generation and coding results concern models trained with the FTP objective and do not test the claimed uninduced look-ahead mechanism.
record.test_reason: Weak test. Section 5.2 probes a frozen next-token GPT2-like model's top-layer state for tokens 2–5 ahead. That bears on V2, but the results appear only in Fig. 6a with no readable numbers. The paper is mainly about its own FTP training method, whose future-token information is induced by training.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that FTP embeddings change smoothly and predict tokens beyond one ahead better than a standard LM. They also conclude that FTP improves generated-text semantic match, classification and the toy coding task. They suggest it learns a smoothly changing 'world state'.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a specially trained multi-token prediction architecture and uses MLP probes; it does not reproduce rhyme-word interventions or the cited Future Lens method.
record.method_sensitivity: The future-token prediction measurement varies by prediction distance (1 to 5 tokens ahead); the paper says FTP performs considerably better than GPT-like models but supplies the plotted values only.

fits_no_version.finding: Training with a discounted 8-token future-prediction objective gives top-layer embeddings that predict future tokens better than GPT embeddings (Fig. 6), vary more smoothly across positions (Fig. 5), and improve topic adherence (0.2502 vs 0.2226 cosine) and toy coding accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An explicit multi-token training objective increases the future-token information carried in single hidden states, compared with next-token training.

record.problems: The future-token perplexities in Fig. 6 are not tabulated, and no chance/reference baseline or uncertainty is stated. The models are small and had not fully converged. The study does not causally intervene on representations.
record.rows_left_out: Section 5.2, Fig. 6b reports future-token prediction by trained transformer decoders, but those decoders use additional decoder context and therefore are not single-hidden-state measurements. Other generation, classification, and coding results concern the FTP training objective rather than the claim's uninduced mechanism.

untested.parts: No rhyme or verse task, and no intervention.
No readable decodability values. No baseline beyond the FTP comparison. No causal test.
No test of whether a next-token model computes features for later positions; the future objective in FTP is imposed by training.
No reasoning, chess or Sokoban look-ahead analysis. The grid-program coding task compares training objectives, not internal look-ahead.
No test of how far apparent plans reach in an untrained-for-it model, or whether they are local heuristics.

missing.what: The GPT model's native 1-token-ahead perplexity from its LM head, the reference against which probe perplexities 2–5 ahead would be judged. Not recorded as a row.

Fig. 6b: a teacher-forced decoder that cross-attends only to the single frozen GPT top-layer embedding, predicting tokens 1–5 ahead. This is declared in rows_left_out, but it is close to a single-state decodability measure and may merit rows.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint. The models are small (about 92M encoder parameters) and not converged. The only V2-relevant evidence is the GPT-model probe rows (r1–r4), which are unreadable from the text, so no verdict is given. The Fig. 6a axis reaches 800, which suggests GPT probe perplexities far above FTP's, but exact values cannot be read.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyme-planning task or intervention on candidate rhyme words.
No tabulated probe perplexities or stated chance/reference level; the study does not test whether the decoded future information causally affects intermediate text.
The study trains FTP models with an explicit future-token objective; it does not test whether a next-token-only model computes features for later positions rather than as a side effect.
No open-weight rhyme-planning test or open attribution-graph tool.
No test of naturally occurring look-ahead in multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban.
No intervention tests whether future-token information steers generation, or whether apparent plans are local heuristics.
